mid = (4+6) DIV 2 = 5, value 12, so return index 5 [1].

k.q: Trace this sorted-array binary search and predict the returned index.
k.code:
array values = [2,4,6,8,10,12,14]
target = 12
low = 0
high = 6
found = -1
while low <= high AND found == -1
    mid = (low + high) DIV 2
    if values[mid] == target then
        found = mid
    elseif values[mid] < target then
        low = mid + 1
    else
        high = mid - 1
    endif
endwhile
print(found)
p: Change target to 2; predict the index.
Explain why an unsorted input would make this algorithm unreliable.
k.a: Target 12 returns index 5. Target 2 returns index 0. Binary search discards halves according to sorted order; an unsorted list breaks that reasoning.
